question: Ravon, Oscar, Aditi, Tyrone, and Kim play a card game. Each person is given \(2\) cards out of a set of \(10\) cards numbered \(1,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(\dots,\) \(10.\) The score of a player is the sum of the numbers of their cards. The scores of the players are as follows: Ravon--\(11,\) Oscar--\(4,\) Aditi--\(7,\) Tyrone--\(16,\) Kim--\(17.\) Which of the following statements is true?
solution:
The smallest scores allow very few card pairs, so finding those pairs first will restrict Ravon's cards.

To score \(4\) with two different cards, Oscar must receive \(1\) and \(3\). The sum \(2+2\) is impossible because there is only one card numbered \(2\).

The possible pairs for Aditi's score of \(7\) are
\[
1+6,\quad 2+5,\quad 3+4.
\]
Oscar already has cards \(1\) and \(3\), so Aditi must receive \(2\) and \(5\).

Now consider every possible pair giving Ravon's score of \(11\):
\[
1+10,\quad 2+9,\quad 3+8,\quad 4+7,\quad 5+6.
\]
All except \(4+7\) use a card already assigned to Oscar or Aditi. Thus Ravon receives cards \(4\) and \(7\).

Ravon was given card \(4\), so the answer is \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
